clue.text: Win honour at international, even losing final point

indicators.note: losing its final point means the word gives up its last letter, a compass point

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour
I is the abbreviation for international
taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A sportsman wins an honour at international level despite dropping a point at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is loose: the letter for 'at' comes before the honour although the clue names them the other way round. Compass points (N, S, E, W) are a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve a goal is to win or attain it through effort.

clue.text: Church is partly against wine

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church

indicators.note: only a part of the word is used, here its opening letter

parts.note: one letter of the word is

explanation.surface: The church partly disapproves of drinking wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Enraged buccaneer loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

explanation.surface: A furious pirate is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym of angry or furious.

clue.text: Sparkling French wine's initially tasty when eating bar nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order
something eating another takes it inside itself
initially points to the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A wine critic praises a French wine that is tasty when drunk with bar snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of wine's attaches the tasty letter to the wine, so it trails after the container is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrant and sparkling both describe something lively and full of energy.

clue.text: Describe party or dance

indicators.note: letters that dance move about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to describe a party or a dance they went to.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to depict or represent it in words or pictures.

clue.text: Directives for religious communities

definitions.meaning: second meaning: monastic brotherhoods such as the Benedictines

explanation.surface: Rules issued to monasteries and convents.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both commands given and monastic societies living under a common rule.

clue.text: Made up account for high society Conservative

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A fabricated story about a Conservative in high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High society' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an exaggerated, unlikely tale, a fabricated account.

clue.text: Corrupt retailer loses right to workshop

indicators.note: corrupt things are altered and twisted, so the letters are reworked
losing an R means the abbreviation for right is removed

parts.note: taken as written, then one R goes

explanation.surface: A dishonest shopkeeper forfeits the right to his workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a workroom.

clue.text: Haughty greeting to German worker may end badly

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
might is the past form of may

indicators.note: end points to the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A greeting to a German worker could end in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End badly' looks like a whole phrase about things going wrong, but only supplies the last letter of badly.
explanation.definitionFit: High and mighty is an idiom for arrogant or overbearing, behaving superior to others.

clue.text: Son gets in by means of travel permit

indicators.note: one item getting in puts it inside the other word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son enters a country using his travel permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement allowing entry to a foreign country.

clue.text: Note to girl to call back leads nowhere

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a path that leads nowhere

indicators.note: back says the word is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A note asking a girl to call back goes unanswered.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind alley is a dead end, a street or course of action going nowhere.

clue.text: Some prefer to change "lass" to "girl"

parts.note: surface padding, part of the hiding sentence

indicators.note: some of the following words means a portion of their letters is taken

parts.note: inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Some people would rather swap the word lass for girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words look like the substitution the clue is about; the answer straddles the end of change and the start of lass.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Has doctor in over joint trouble

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
in a down-style flip, over says the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Someone has the doctor in again over a troublesome joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship means suffering or difficulty, a kind of trouble.

clue.text: Library has entire novel on Casanova, for example

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: LIB is a short form of library

explanation.surface: A library stocks a complete novel about Casanova.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, the Venetian adventurer, is the archetypal libertine, a man of dissolute sexual habits.

clue.text: Street mix medley embraces radical views

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: one who embraces radical views

indicators.note: a medley is a jumble of mixed parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medley of street music adopts politically radical themes.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist is a person who holds fanatical political or religious opinions.

clue.text: Huge crowd reported at store

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so the word heard is spelt differently

parts.note: a horde is a huge crowd

explanation.surface: Reports of a huge crowd at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' looks like a shop where the crowd gathers, but it is the verb or noun for a stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a hidden stockpile; to hoard is to store things away.

clue.text: Teases ladies' club entering bike races

indicators.note: entering means going inside the other piece

parts.note: the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

explanation.surface: Members of a women's club get teased when they turn up at motorbike races.
explanation.definitionFit: To twit someone is to tease or taunt them.

clue.text: Cranks or royal house?

parts.note: to crank a handle is to wind it

explanation.surface: A playful question: are these eccentrics or the royal family?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cranks' reads as eccentric people, but it is the verb meaning turns a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor is the name of the reigning British royal house since 1917.

clue.text: Making use of tactic embraced by oriental dynasty

parts.note: E for East, as oriental means eastern

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside it

explanation.surface: A Chinese dynasty adopting a particular strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriental supplies only the compass letter, which sits at the front of the dynasty before the tactic goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Employing something means using it or putting it to work.

clue.text: For England player, endless blame is standard against Germany

indicators.note: without either end, so only the middle of the word remains

parts.note: blame without its first and last letters
par is the standard or norm
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An England footballer faces endless blame for a standard match against Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Lampard was an England midfielder; the surface nods to England's 2010 World Cup match against Germany, when his goal was wrongly disallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Lampard played midfield for England, scoring 29 international goals.

clue.text: Can't be famous?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words: unable to do something
second meaning: well known or remarkable

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as someone doubting they can become famous; read as two words, the answer means cannot.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole it means noteworthy or eminent; split in two it means unable.

clue.text: Counsel DA about corruption

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: Legal advice to a district attorney concerning a corruption case.
explanation.walkthrough: A DA is an American district attorney, which the surface uses as the prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to give them guidance, which is a synonym of advice.

clue.text: Sub-woofer not expected to succeed?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: one not expected to succeed

parts.note: sub- is a prefix meaning under

explanation.surface: A subwoofer loudspeaker is unlikely to win.
explanation.walkthrough: A subwoofer is a bass loudspeaker; split, sub and woofer become two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The underdog is the competitor who is expected to lose a contest.

clue.text: Make record of tune I'm composing

indicators.note: composing means arranging, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A composer records the tune they are writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To minute a meeting is to write an official record of what was said.

clue.text: Dig, mixing dung with earth

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: A gardener digs, mixing manure into the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like gardening, but it means a poke in the ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dig is a poke with the elbow, which is a nudge.

clue.text: Adapts iris to become indoor plant

indicators.note: to become something else the letters must change their arrangement

explanation.surface: An iris plant adapts so that it can be grown indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adapts' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy houseplant, famously common in Victorian parlours.

clue.text: Died with bad bet money due

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A gambler died owing money after a bad bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is a sum of money owed to someone.

clue.text: Healthier to have resistance to fried food

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it inside

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Being healthier means resisting fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' reads as willpower, but it is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A fritter is a piece of fruit, vegetable or meat coated in batter and deep-fried.

clue.text: Heard about journalist being held

indicators.note: about means around and about, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Rumours were heard about a journalist being held captive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that adhered stuck fast, so it held to a surface.
